title: Your event plan, your offer and your first 90 days

say: Your event plan, your offer, and your first 90 days.
This is the video for module four of Catering Basics and Food Safety: your event plan, your offer and your next steps.
Your capstone is one complete plan for a real or realistic event. It should be good enough that another trained cook could follow it and deliver the job safely.

say: Professional kitchens use a system called HACCP. Its thinking is simple. For each step, ask what could go wrong, what stops it, and how you will check.
Funmi plans 9 kilograms of coleslaw for 100 guests. Coleslaw is never cooked, so every step matters. She buys firm, fresh vegetables and salad cream with an intact seal and a valid date.

panel.heading: Funmi's safety plan for coleslaw
items: Buy: firm vegetables, sealed salad cream
Prepare: safe water, green board, clean hands
Store: covered, in the fridge below 5°C
Mix: dress on the morning, keep chilled
Transport: own cooler with ice; log 4°C

say: She washes the vegetables in safe water, uses the green ready-to-eat board, and washes her hands first.

say: Clients hear my food is delicious from every caterer. Vague words do not win bookings.
Specific details do, because a client can check them. Use only photos of your own food, in daylight, and testimonials with permission. Never use internet photos of other caterers' food.
Ngozi replies within the hour. She thanks the client and asks for the date, venue, serving time, format and any allergies.
Package A is jollof, chicken, moi moi and coleslaw, at about 4,200 naira per head. For 70 guests that is 294,000 naira.
Package B is fried rice, turkey, plantain and salad, at about 5,500 per head, or 385,000 naira.
She adds that food is held above 60 degrees in insulated coolers and that they arrive at least one hour before serving. She offers a paid tasting and states the 50% deposit to confirm the date.
Amaka finishes the course with no paid jobs yet. In days 1 to 30, she does two test cooks for family events, buys a probe thermometer and a second cooler, and finalises her offer.

say: Keep business money in a separate account or wallet. When you grow, ask CAC about registering a business name, NAFDAC if you package food for shops, and your local environmental health office about permits.

say: To remember. Six parts make one complete plan. For every step, name the hazard, the control and the check. Specific, honest offers win bookings.
Cook to 70 degrees, hold above 60 or below 5, and never more than 2 hours at room temperature. Then test, deliver small, review and grow.

say: Now practise. Draft hazard and control tables for your two highest-risk dishes, and do a small test cook with a temperature log. Create your one-page offer with your own food photo. And write your 90-day plan.
